history.period: 15th–16th century (one source claims Chola-period 11th-century origins — CONFLICT (verify))
history.summary: Samadhi-temple of Tontada Siddalinga, a revered 15th-century Veerashaiva/Lingayat saint who performed 12 years of penance in a garden (thota) at Yediyur, attained Nirvikalpa Shivayoga Samadhi here, and is venerated as an incarnation of Shiva. The gaddige (samadhi) is a heap of vibhuti (sacred ash) in linga form crowned by a metallic processional image. The large north-facing Dravidian temple with its gopuram depicts scenes from the saint's life; his 701 Vachanas are collected in the Shathsthala Jnana Saramrutha. It is a major Lingayat pilgrimage centre; free food and accommodation are offered to visitors. Renovated in 2012.

name: Siddhalingeshwara Temple, Yediyur
town_description: Yediyur (Yedeyur) is a town in Kunigal taluk of Tumkur district, about 19 km from Kunigal and 95 km from Bengaluru, lying on the Bangalore-Mangalore highway (NH-75). It is an important pilgrimage centre for the Lingayat faith, serving as both temple and tomb of the saint Siddalinga Shivayogi. Shops and small restaurants cluster around the temple. (CSV town 'Tumkur' is approximate — the temple is at Yediyur, Kunigal Taluk.)

travel.road: On the Bangalore–Mangalore highway (NH-75), 95 km from Bengaluru and 18 km from Kunigal; well connected by KSRTC buses between Bangalore and Tumkur/Kunigal.
